subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single static TypeScript vehicle model, an armored riot truck roughly 5.2m long, 2.4m wide, 2.5m tall, facing +Z with four large wheels and no joints needed.

Now I'm detailing the design: a frustum lower hull, cab, roof light bars with neon glow, a water cannon turret with barrel, rear tank with fictional corp decals ("KANTOR-VEX SECURITY"), underglow strips, bull bar, antennas, and tinted windows with a glowing HUD. I'm keeping the API usage safe by sticking to box/cylinder geometry and the kit's glow helper rather than riskier builder functions, limiting myself to a small flat color palette, and working out coordinates so wheels sit at radius 0.55 with their centers at y=0.55, and the chassis spans from y=0.5 to 1.5.

I'm laying out the vehicle front-to-back from z=-2.7 to 2.7: a lower hull box with armor paneling, a front hood box, and an extruded upper body profile (rear vertical, roofline, windshield slope, hood slope) to form the cab shape with custom paint. Now I'm working out how to add the windshield as a thin rotated box angled along that same slope.

Working out the glowing window plane with a cyan-lined texture, oriented to face outward after the rotation so it reads correctly against the tilted panel.

Now I'm adding side windows on the X-facing surfaces, then building roof light bars with alternating red/blue/white glow boxes inside a dark housing.

I'm designing the roof-mounted water cannon turret with a lathe-based base and barrel, plus a glowing cyan nozzle tip, and reworking the body so the cab is shorter and a rear tank section fits behind it.

I'm sizing the rear tank as a horizontal cylinder with painted stripe decals on its sides, adjusting its radius and position so it sits slightly above the cab roof, and refining the cab's back wall and profile to match.

I'll add straps around the tank as thin disc-shaped lathe rings at a few z-offsets to simulate hazard bands, positioned so they wrap the tank surface without disrupting the cab area.

Now I'm working out wheel placement — considering whether to use 4 or 6 wheels and spacing their axles along the z-axis to fit under the cab and tank sections.

Each wheel gets a dark tire cylinder, a glowing neon hub ring, and bolt details, with the x-offset tuned so the wheel width extends just outside the hull width without clipping through the body panels.

I'm working out how to add fender arches over the wheels using a partial cylinder cut with an open angle, weighing whether to leave it open-ended or closed with end caps so the outer curved surface reads correctly from outside the car.

Deciding to simplify by using angled boxes for the fenders instead of fighting cylinder rotation math, then moving on to design the front bumper area—a ram/bull bar made from a box with vertical rods and a neon strip, plus a wedge-shaped cow catcher extruded as a trapezoid profile near the front of the hood.

Now I'm adding glowing headlight boxes near the front corners, a magenta DRL strip across the hood, and bull bar tubes as swept curves, then planning neon accent strips along the lower body sides and underglow near the bottom, keeping them mostly hidden but present for lighting effect.

I'm now setting up a texture panel on the cab's side faces to display "RIOT SUPPRESSION UNIT" branding text, working through the correct plane placement and orientation so the text reads properly from a viewer positioned off to the side.

I'm planning a branded sign panel on the hull with fictional corporate text, then adding rear details like taillights, a plate, roof hatch, antenna array, a camera dome with a glowing eye, and LRAD speaker horns, plus mirrors and side steps for extra detail.

For the paint, I'm defining a cyberpunk gunmetal palette with magenta, cyan, yellow, red, and blue accents, using panel seams and grime wear patterns built from procedural noise functions, plus hazard stripe decals and hex-vent textures, aiming for roughly 150 parts total.

Now I'm building helper functions for boxes and glowing parts, keeping flat colors for anything emissive since painted glow isn't allowed, and limiting the distinct color count to stay under thirty. I'm working out the rear end geometry next — taillights, bumper, and a rear door texture plane — figuring out the correct facing direction and axis orientation so it reads correctly from behind the vehicle.

Still working out panel orientations...

Adding wheel glow disks, hub caps, and bolt rings positioned around each wheel, then moving on to think about the roof light bar placement.

Then a holo-banner decal on the tank side. For the water cannon, I'm placing a turret base on the roof behind the light bar, with a swiveling body, a tapered barrel extending forward and up, and a flared nozzle with a glowing cyan ring at the tip, plus a side hose connecting it.

I'm adding support rods between turret and barrel, a camera pod underneath, a small gauge texture on the turret side, and a glowing cyan water-level stripe along the tank's sides near the rear.

Now I'm planning out the set of SVG textures needed: HUD window, side sign, logo decal, gauge, vents, rear panel, plus hazard stripe paint. I'm sketching a corporate emblem design for the logo—a hexagon with a stylized letter and a fictional brand name, something like "VANTA".

Writing paint shader code...

Still refining the hood and cab geometry...

Adding more trim details...

I'll settle on a single wide window spanning the cab side, rendered with dark glass and cyan reflection streaks, plus a small sign panel positioned on the lower hull near the side neon strip.

Now adding roof details: antenna rods at the rear, lathe-shaped speaker horns mounted on either side of the roof facing forward, and a small camera dome sphere near the turret position.

I'm placing the side mirrors as box arms extending from the cab front with glowing strips, keeping the tank cradle within the body's existing bounds, and considering simple rod-based rear ladder details plus a lathe-shaped valve cap at the tank's rear end.

Now I'm adding glowing red taillight strips and a magenta neon bar across the rear bumper, then routing a curved hose with a swept cross-section arching from the tank's front to the turret base using a sequence of control points for a natural dip and rise.

Writing armor paint shader...

Adding diagonal paint stripes...

Now I'm designing the tank paint scheme with white-grey base and blue bands, plus the logo decal placement—a hexagon with a cyan V shape and text, positioned on the tank sides with mirroring logic for correct orientation when viewed from either side.

I'm worried about text mirroring issues on decals, so I'll simplify the logo to just the symbol without text to avoid risk. For the sign, I'm drafting dark background text with magenta border and neon cyan lettering, but skipping CJK characters since font rendering support is uncertain—sticking to ASCII instead.

Now I'm working through the turret geometry, checking that the gauge dial, side mounting planes, barrel, light bar, and nozzle all fit together with correct offsets and clearances across the many parts of this model.

Finalizing the lathe call for the tank with proper axis and position, adding glowing magenta grille slits on the hull front, then I'm ready to write the final code.
